---
title: "Penguins dashboard"
subtitle: "RaukR 2026 · Day 2 — Dashboards demo"
format: dashboard
---

<!--
Day-2 "Demos — if time" artifact. A self-contained, STATIC `format: dashboard`
page: no Shiny/OJS backend, so it opens as plain HTML anywhere. The teaching point is the
LAYOUT MODEL (rows, valueboxes, a card, a tabset), not plot color — the RaukR brand is
monochrome teal and can't separate three species by hue (see the Day-1 payoff figure), so the
plots keep ggplot's default fills; the brand carries through the dashboard *chrome* (header,
fonts, valuebox color) via the project `_brand.yml`.
-->

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggokabeito)   # color-blind-safe (Okabe-Ito) scale, same as Day 1
data(penguins)
penguins <- penguins |> filter(!is.na(bill_len), !is.na(bill_dep), !is.na(body_mass))
```

<!-- `##` starts a row, `###` a column; the heading text ("Row"/"Column") is just a label. -->
## Row {height="20%"}

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Species"
# icon = any name from the bootstrap-icons set (https://icons.getbootstrap.com);
# color = a brand/theme role ("primary", "secondary", ...) — here the RaukR teal.
list(
  color = "primary",
  icon = "tags",
  value = n_distinct(penguins$species)
)
```

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Penguins measured"
list(
  color = "secondary",
  icon = "clipboard-data",
  value = nrow(penguins)
)
```

## Row {height="80%"}

### Column

<!-- Each code cell becomes a `.card`; its `#| title:` sets the card header. -->

```{r}
#| title: "Body mass by species"
#| fig-alt: "Boxplot of penguin body mass in grams by species; Gentoo is clearly the heaviest, Adelie and Chinstrap overlap around 3,700 g."
ggplot(penguins, aes(species, body_mass, fill = species)) +
  geom_boxplot(show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_okabe_ito() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Body mass (g)")
```

### Column {.tabset}

```{r}
#| title: "Bill scatter"
#| fig-alt: "Scatterplot of bill depth versus bill length in millimeters, colored by species; the three species form separate clusters."
ggplot(penguins, aes(bill_len, bill_dep, color = species)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_okabe_ito() +
  labs(x = "Bill length (mm)", y = "Bill depth (mm)", color = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| title: "Mean measurements"
penguins |>
  summarise(
    bill_len = mean(bill_len),
    bill_dep = mean(bill_dep),
    body_mass = mean(body_mass),
    .by = species
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```
